Each hour: time, direction and speed (knots, g = gust), odds of 12kt or more, regime, waves, tide height in ft with r rising or f falling. OUTFLOW NOT RIDDEN = Squamish outflow, never recommend. OFF DIR = direction does not work at that spot.
Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Sat, Oct 31 7:25am to 6:26pm; Sun, Nov 1 6:26am to 5:25pm; Mon, Nov 2 6:28am to 5:23pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Sat, Oct 31 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Light morning, but the outflow is building. Pam Rocks is up to N 16 at 9am from 13 at 7am, Pemberton is now 2 hPa above Vancouver and climbing, and Environment Canada calls Howe Sound northerly 20 to 30 by early evening. The page hasn't caught it yet.

So Porteau is my late maybe, about 3:30pm to last light around 6:15pm, on the ebb down to 11.9ft at 5:34pm. Check before driving: if Pam Rocks reads 22 or more from the north by 2:30pm, go.

Backup is Tsawwassen south side, 3pm to 6pm, NW 9 to 10, advanced riders only

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PCT 31 October 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Sunday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 10 to 20 knots increasing to northerly outflow 20 to 30 early this evening then diminishing to northerly outflow 5 to 15 near noon Sunday.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 AM PCT 31 October 2026): Today Tonight and Sunday. Wind east 5 to 15 knots becoming light late this morning then becoming northwest 10 to 15 late this afternoon. Wind diminishing to light Sunday morning then becoming southeast 10 Sunday evening.
